To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the unstable state is an effective way to improve the four-point walking pattern assisted by FES.
the unstable state of walking can be induced in paraplegics by FES and that the horizontal displacement of COB in the unstable state is significantly larger than in the stable phase of walking.
the FES assisted four-point gait is a viable method to increase walking speed of paraplegics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of the control system for a four-point gait using functional electrical stimulation ( FES ) for the paralysed lower limbs.
the design of the FES system, the control of the system and the evaluation of the system.
the development of a novel FES-assisted four-point gait.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
functional electrical stimulation (fes) improves the walking ability of paraplegics.
the use of FES and crutches for walking can be improved by introducing the passive phase of walking.
FES can be applied to assist the paraplegic patient in the walking process by providing an additional support in the form of a passive unstable phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unstable state can be used as an effective tool for the control of FES-assisted four-point gait.
the unstable state of walking can be achieved by FES and crutches.
FES can be used to improve the four-point gait by inducing unstable state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the unstable state can be achieved in the paraplegic gait pattern.
FES-assisted four-point gait is possible with the use of unstable state and that the unstable phase is a key factor in the gait pattern.
